editorial.headline: The Boundaries of In-House Professional Certification
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers an organisation certifying the professional competence of its own employees or students—nationally open to full foreign ownership, while Bali requires address-level risk verification.
editorial.body:
Professional certification can imply a broad public-facing credentialing business. This activity is more defined than that. It covers measuring and certifying the work or professional competence of an organisation’s own employees or students. Its centre of gravity is internal assessment: the people being assessed belong to the employer or education-and-training setting carrying out the certification.

That distinction matters for the practical identity of the activity. The certification is first-party certification, conducted for the organisation’s own workforce or learners rather than described here as a service for an outside population. The supplied record does not specify any business-scale categories open to this activity, so it provides no basis for assigning it to a particular scale.

At the national level, the position is straightforward. The activity is open to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, the record permits full foreign ownership nationally. Its cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership cap in the record to qualify that national position.

Bali adds a more careful operational reading, but not a prohibition. The provincial PMA moratorium permanently and island-wide blocks low and medium-low risk activities; this activity is recorded as medium-high or high risk and is therefore not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`. That is not a blank cheque for any location: the record expressly calls for verification by address. For a foreign-owned registration, the honest conclusion is that the activity remains available in Bali, subject to confirming the risk treatment at the proposed address.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, full foreign ownership is permitted; in Bali, the activity is not moratorium-blocked but its treatment must still be verified by address.
